correctness.rationale: Independent reconstitution of the five-by-five rational limiting Jacobian yields the exact stated degree-five characteristic polynomial (symbolic determinant equality). First-order expansion of the two-fast-state Schur complement gives Q=1+tau_f eps z+eps²z²/(alpha gamma) and determinant perturbation -153000(400z-1)(s+5) tau_f eps, checked symbolically, not inferred from finite-K fits. The positive isolated large quartic root t=116.3626739461 leads to s_H(∞)=13.016079814889247 and omega=10.7871531900729. The eigenvalue implicit derivative gives c=670.0071181534648>0 and frequency d=4.00432112186999; fixed alpha,beta,gamma>0 and matched conserved total 91+50tau_f/K are essential. The result is local near the specified simple Hopf point, not a global assertion about all Hopf bifurcations. The paper also supplies rational sign intervals and transverse stability; finite spectral samples alone would not establish this conclusion.

value.rationale: In enzyme-sharing reaction networks, introducing a fast intermediate is a natural model refinement. The sign, explicit nonzero leading sensitivity and reduction of three arbitrary fast rates to a residence-time factor distinguish qualitative Hopf persistence from a useful parameter recalibration. A model-specific exact perturbation is motivated by the benchmark and is not merely a restatement of persistence.

limitations: Fixed alpha,beta,gamma positive, concentration-matched total; only the local Hopf branch; no global or arbitrary-K stability claim.
